$comment: Copy this file to config/local.config.json and edit. local.config.json is gitignored.
This is a JSON file and NOT a dotfile on purpose. See DECISIONS.md: a global permission
hook freezes background agents for hours on any path matching .env*, so this project has
no .env of any kind. API keys, when a free-tier source needs one, go under
adapters.<id>.options.
Relative paths are resolved against the repository root.
toolkitRoot: folder holding the external tools (venv/, bin/, blackbird/, data/). Leave empty to
auto-detect: OSINT_TOOLKIT_ROOT env var, then ./osint-kit, ./tools/osint-kit, ~/osint-kit.
opsecKitRoot: optional metadata-scrubber checkout (Scrub view). Empty = OSINT_OPSEC_KIT_ROOT, then ./opsec-kit, ../opsec-kit, ~/opsec-kit.
globalConcurrency: total child processes in flight across all adapters.
defaultConcurrencyPerAdapter: cap for one adapter, so a slow site-sweeper cannot
starve everything else.
defaultTimeoutMs: a tool that has not exited by now is killed (process tree, not just
the parent). OSINT CLIs hang on dead endpoints constantly; this is not optional.
maxOutputBytes: hard cap on captured stdout+stderr per run. Beyond it the capture is
truncated and flagged, rather than filling RAM.
Per-adapter overrides, keyed by adapter id. Every key is optional.
enabled       - false hides the adapter from the UI entirely
concurrency   - overrides defaultConcurrencyPerAdapter
minIntervalMs - minimum gap between two starts of THIS adapter. This is the
politeness knob: it is what stops a username sweep from looking
like an attack to the sites being queried.
timeoutMs     - overrides defaultTimeoutMs
bin           - absolute path to the binary/script when it is not on PATH
options       - free-form knobs the adapter reads, including any API keys
The deep username tool. Slow and rate-limit-prone: it reported bot-protection
errors on a 38-site run. topSites is the knob that matters; allSites is minutes.
bin defaults to <toolkitRoot>/venv/Scripts/maigret.exe.
The fast username tool. Constrain it with `sites` or it probes thousands.
Note: sherlock's --json flag LOADS a site database; it has no JSON output.
Prefers <toolkitRoot>/venv-bb, because its requirements.txt pins exact versions
and downgrades packages maigret depends on. Create it with:
py -3.12 -m venv <toolkitRoot>\venv-bb
<toolkitRoot>\venv-bb\Scripts\pip.exe install -r <toolkitRoot>\blackbird\requirements.txt
`bin` here means the PYTHON INTERPRETER, not blackbird.py.
updateSites=true re-downloads the site list on every run and makes results
non-reproducible; it is off by default on purpose.
Rate limiting is its normal outcome, not an exception — every module returned a
rate-limit result during Phase 0 from this IP. A rate-limited site is UNCHECKED,
never 'no account'. noPasswordRecovery=true avoids sending the subject a reset
email, at the cost of most of its coverage.
Runs from <toolkitRoot>/venv-th — it needs Python >= 3.14, the inverse of the
3.12 the rest of the toolbelt uses. The default source list is the eight that
need no API key. Its exit code is 0 even when every source fails; read the
per-source findings instead.
Works with zero API keys. The adapter always passes -config and -pc pointing at
<toolkitRoot>/config/ so subfinder does not write to AppData.
Free-tier keys (GitHub is genuinely free) widen coverage; add them to
<toolkitRoot>/config/subfinder-provider-config.yaml, not here.
Offline. The binary must stay beside its exiftool_files\ directory, and the
shipped exiftool(-k).exe must be renamed to exiftool.exe — the (-k) suffix makes
it wait for a keypress, which would hang the spawn forever.
Always runs in --simulate mode: it resolves the listing and downloads nothing.
cookiesFile points at a Netscape-format cookie jar for sites that need a login;
without one, Instagram and most of X return an authentication error.
Free, keyless, no install. matchType is 'domain' for a domain entity and 'exact'
for a URL; collapse=digest shows only the captures whose content differs.
Verified 2026-08-30: Reddit now answers HTTP 403 with a 'blocked by network
security' page for every keyless .json endpoint from an ordinary connection, and
a browser User-Agent is refused identically. The adapter reports that as a
refusal aimed at us and concludes nothing about the account. Keep the honest
User-Agent; faking a browser does not help and makes the app a worse citizen.
requestGapMs is the politeness gap between pages.
Needs a candidate password per run: options.password (hashed locally; only the
first five hex characters of the SHA-1 are ever sent) or options.sha1.
Do NOT put a real password in this file — it is gitignored but still plaintext on
disk, and check() will warn you about it.
No network at all. Re-reads the raw captures already in the case folder, so it
costs nothing and gets better every time a different adapter runs.
The only adapter that can act on a name. It reads the case's own entities.json and
welds the subject to every other seed — name + town, name + school, name + handle —
because a bare name is a join key, not a query.
Measured from this machine on 2026-09-03, with the app's honest User-Agent:
html.duckduckgo.com/html/   200, ~32 kB, 9-10 parseable results.  WORKS
lite.duckduckgo.com/lite/   200, same index, different markup.    WORKS
wiby.me/json/               200, real keyless JSON, tiny index.   WORKS
public SearXNG instances    2 of 80 answered format=json at all.  MOSTLY DEAD
www.mojeek.com/search       200 with a JavaScript captcha page.   DEAD
api.qwant.com/v3            403.                                  DEAD
search.brave.com            429 on the first request, and its API now needs a
payment card even on the free plan.  OUT OF SCOPE
api.marginalia.nu / api2    timeout / 404 on every documented path. DEAD
DuckDuckGo's limiter is bursty rather than a fixed rate: it served a CAPTCHA on the
third query of a run at 6-second spacing, and served forty in a row on another day.
That CAPTCHA arrives as HTTP 202, not an error, so it is detected from the body and
reported as a refusal — never as 'no results'. Once it fires, the whole host is
struck off for the rest of the run and the chain falls through.
backends: the chain, in order. 'searxng' is deliberately NOT in the default: the one
public instance that answered reliably searches only the FIRST WORD of the query
and ignores site: entirely, returning a confident page of results for a question
nobody asked. Add it only with an instance you trust, ideally your own.
instances: SearXNG base URLs, tried in order, when 'searxng' is in the chain.
requestGapMs: politeness gap between requests. Raise it, never lower it.
maxQueries: how many combinations one run spends. The list is ordered strongest
first, so a smaller number simply drops the weakest queries.
queries: run these literal strings instead of deriving any.
Search operators, prepared and explained. Shares the engine chain with websearch.
mode: 'open' builds the library and makes NO request at all — the right setting for
an air-gapped or deliberately quiet session. 'run' executes and parses. 'both'
(default) runs the top few and hands over the rest as URLs to open.
engine: which engine the open-me URLs point at. Google honours filetype:, inurl:
and long OR chains best, which is why it is the default for looking rather than
parsing. 'duckduckgo', 'bing' and 'google-images' also work.
dorks: restrict to named template ids (see support/dorks.ts).
maxRun: how many runnable dorks one run actually executes.
The other archive. Wayback crawls; archive.today saves only what a person clicked
Save on, rendered in a real browser — so it holds the social media, deleted posts
and edited profiles Wayback mostly misses.
It has no official API and a reputation for needing a browser. Measured 2026-09-03:
the Memento TimeMap at https://archive.ph/timemap/<url> answers 200 with
application/link-format, keyless, with no Cloudflare challenge, and a URL it has
never seen answers a clean 404. Snapshots themselves also fetch fine. No browser
automation is needed and none is used.
The surprise: the honest User-Agent works and a Chrome one does not. Every mirror
answered 200 to 'osint-workbench/0.1 ...' and 429 to a copied Chrome string, seconds
apart. Do not 'fix' this by faking a browser.
Submitting a NEW capture is the one thing that would need a browser, and is
deliberately not implemented: reading an archive is observation, adding to it is
publication.
mirrors: tried in order. All seven are one service behind different domains and
returned byte-identical responses; the list exists for the day DNS or a filter
takes one of them out.
